evals.prompt: evals/files/essay-manual.md is the start of docs/manual.md for mdmost, a terminal Markdown pager. It reads like an essay about the program. Rewrite it so it reads like a reference page. Anything you cut that is still worth knowing goes into a maintainer-notes.md next to it.
evals.expected_output: The manual excerpt rewritten in present tense and third person, with ASCII term lists, and a maintainer-notes.md holding the rationale that came out.
expectations: The rewritten manual has no 'you', 'your', 'we' or 'our' outside code blocks
The rewritten manual contains no em dash anywhere
The option and key lists use the form '- `--option`: description', with the term in a code span followed directly by a colon
The phrases 'so the two cannot drift apart' and 'which is what makes it usable for' no longer appear in the manual
The reasoning about rendering being a pure function of its inputs, or about why there is no --color flag, appears in maintainer-notes.md instead of being deleted
The level-1 headings NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS and KEYS are all still present, spelled as before

evals.prompt: The install section of our README (evals/files/readme-install.md) has turned into an essay around a handful of commands. Cut it down to what someone installing the tool needs, and keep the explanations somewhere sensible instead of throwing them away.
evals.expected_output: An install section that is the commands per platform, and a maintainer-notes.md with the explanations that came out.
expectations: Every install route (Homebrew, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE, any Linux, Rust) is still present with its commands intact
The paragraphs about Homebrew 6.0 trust and about outdated Command Line Tools are gone from the README
The sentence about fancy-regex versus oniguruma is gone from the README
The removed explanations appear in a maintainer-notes.md
The README contains no em dash anywhere, including the route labels
The README does not praise the tool
